interest: Documents public protests and State Department debates over restricting commercial credits and tracking Japanese gold shipments.
overview: This file documents U.S. State Department monitoring of Japanese finances, war budgets, and foreign credit attempts between January and April 1938 following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese War. It highlights widespread public protests against American loans to Japan, internal State-Treasury deliberations on credit restrictions under the Neutrality Act, and intelligence tracking Japanese gold shipments and foreign exchange reserves.
